sources: CRA — GST/HST information for taxi operators and commercial ride-sharing drivers (canada.ca, page details 2026-08-31) · current · commercial ride-sharing drivers must register for GST/HST even if they are small suppliers; tax is usually already included in the fares; ITCs on GST/HST paid on gasoline, repairs, maintenance, washes, vehicle leases/purchases; no ITCs on insurance or interest

CRA — GST/HST Memorandum 2-2 Small suppliers (canada.ca, updated June 2026) · current · the $30,000 small supplier threshold does not apply to ride-sharing; other (e.g. delivery-only) suppliers generally register once taxable sales pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration possible

Calculation (not a CRA rule): b14/calc.py → data.json. Manitoba, 2026, GST 5%. $20,000 fares incl. GST → GST inside = 20,000 × 5/105 = $952.38; gas + repairs for the rides $4,200 incl. GST → ITC 4,200 × 5/105 = $200.00; net to CRA $752.38. Delivery-only, same $20,000 (< $30,000): registration not required → $0. Dependencies: province (HST provinces use a different rate), business-use share of vehicle costs, other taxable sales, voluntary registration, quick method. Income tax is separate. Amounts are an example.

titles: Uber Driver in Canada? You Owe GST From Ride #1
Uber vs DoorDash: Different GST Rules in Canada
yt.description:
Drive for Uber? CRA says commercial ride-sharing drivers must register for GST/HST even as small suppliers. There's no $30,000 pass.

Delivering food only (DoorDash)? Different rule: registration is generally required once taxable sales pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters.

Example (Manitoba, 2026, GST 5%): $20,000 in fares, GST included.
• GST inside: 20,000 × 5/105 = about $952
• GST paid on gas and repairs for the rides comes back as input tax credits: $200 here
• Insurance and loan interest: no GST credit
• Net to CRA: about $752
Same $20,000 delivering food only: no GST registration required.

Which app do you drive for? Uber or DoorDash? Tell me below.

Sources: CRA 'GST/HST information for taxi operators and commercial ride-sharing drivers'; CRA GST/HST Memorandum 2-2 (Small suppliers). Example only; general information, not tax advice.
